newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges PLO negotiator to rethink resignation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges PLO negotiator to rethink resignation.

text.p: A senior U.S. official on Monday expressed concern at the resignation of PLO chief negotiator Mahmoud Abbas from PLO-Israeli talks and urged Abbas to reconsider.

"Obviously it's a sign of concern when someone of his (Abbas') stature tenders his resigntion. We hope he would reconsider it. We know how frustrated the Palestinians are right now. We sympathise with that," said the official who declined to be named.

Abbas handed Palestinian President Yasser Arafat his resignation after a tough meeting with Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy late on Sunday, in protest against what he considered Israeli intransigence.

PLO officials have been angered by the Israeli government's decision to build a Jewish settlement in occupied East Jerusalem and to pull out from nine percent of the West Bank and not 30 percent as the Palestinians had expected.
The U.S. administration criticised the decision to build the settlement but vetoed a United Nation's resolution last week which called on Israel to abandon its plans.
U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the U.S. urged Palestinians and Israelis to solve their problems through negotiations.
Israel said that an American letter attached to the Hebron redeployment protocol stated that Israel alone decides the scope of further redeployments from the West Bank.
"I think it's best to let them continue to discuss that without injecting the United States into that debate," Burns told reporters at the State Department briefing on Monday.
